title: The "one shot" posts are becoming ridiculous.
author: No_Departure7494
selftext:
No wonder why some people are disappointed by what AI can do, they're using Forza Horizon 6 clips for clickbait and stating "Opus 5.5 made this overnight!".

Just for the sake of experimentation, has anyone here successfully one shotted anything worth playing?

comments.author: Fizassist1
comments.body: lol no.  all of my games have taken a fair amount of iteration, and they are basically arcade games and simple 3d

comments.author: romansamurai
comments.body: Yeah I think mods should ban any one shot or “Claude did this in n hours” posts.

comments.author: I_pee_in_shower
comments.body:
They feed into the retardation and the hysteria

My last game is not finished and took hundreds of prompts over weeks and I’m very experienced

replies.author: Pixeltoir
replies.body: IKR??? I keep on prompting and fixing bugs and kept asking myself if there's something wrong in the way I prompt since I was not able to "one-shot" my game idea

replies.author: Ok-Sea300
replies.body:
You forgot to add "run in a loop until its perfect bro, no mistakes so its super sweet bro"

Yes I know, its dumb but you have to call claude bro, it's the secret code to unlock free mythos.

Obviously kidding. Oneshot games are fun for 8 seconds and then the novelty wears off.

replies.author: True_Woodpecker2118
replies.body: Im brand new with no experiance. And my "beta" has gone through atleast 100

comments.author: dilberry
comments.body: 100% - there should be heavy criteria for posting 1 shot posts .. youtube video and bounce should = banned IMO. Especially if the OP is straight up lying or paid shilling.

comments.author: apra24
comments.body:
Its basically a "one shot" where they deliberately planned everything up front, with self evaluation.

But no one-shot will ever be as good as anything built with a human in the loop. You need to try things out constantly, testing what feels right and what doesnt.

replies.author: LoatheCat
replies.body: No, it's just a lie lmao. They're not even doing that.

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: We should ban these one shot posts. They give this sub a terrible name. It’s just a bunch of kids doing the shit too.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: No, we shouldn't ban them, but we should downvote them if they're lazy or if they don't talk about their development process.

comments.author: Pixeltoir
comments.body:
Bro, I've seen a twitter dude said they one-shotted a realistic FPS game

The video show

\*Literal Crysis 1 gameplay\*

comments.author: Sacred_B
comments.body: lel I tried a one shot design approach on a local multiplayer minigolf game with hazards you can place down. It was 3 holes per map, which I found strange, and the flag in the hole had collision so you couldn't actually sink a hole at anything over 0.002 m/s. It was a good lesson to learn. Oh and placing a hazard wasted your first shot so no one ever gets a hole-in-one, you know, the most satisfying thing about minigolf.

replies.author: Meatt
replies.body: I mean, you could just send a second prompt and fix all that.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: I’m pretty anti one shot for my stuff.. but I did oneshot a minigame for my main game kind of . I was super impressed with how quick it built this game but I’m not even sure if it will be efficient because it’s going to take a lot of tuning anyways.

comments.author: InformationTop5376
comments.body: That’s really what the Steam disclosure should be. “Did you one shot prompt this?” Joking of course…

comments.author: CodeWizardCS
comments.body: You can one shot things but the gameplay loop is going to be limited. Up to this point, my initial task is like a one shot that builds a skeleton/vertical slice but it's not really close to a game that I would want to play at that point. It depends on how complex of a game you want to make. You can one shot simple games.

comments.author: Just-Routine967
comments.body:
All the one shot videos are cherry picked, there is no gameplay beyond the limited amount they show, mechanics will be unbalanced and nonsensical. The people saying all you need is a good GDD are full of shit, getting the feel of a game right still requires human oversight and testing with many iterations.

I'd love to check out your game, is it FPS, RTS or what?

comments.author: spixt
comments.body: Those people are 100% being paid by openAI/anthropic to advertise their newest models.

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: I’ve been working on my current game since the beginning of the year, and there’s still a lot to be done. (Although the technology has improved quite a bit in the meantime.)

comments.author: TalkingHeadsVideo
comments.body: Alot are scamers wanting you to subscribe and join thier paid service

comments.author: FabulousCount2009
comments.body: yeah i even dont like them

comments.author: 0_0Luke
comments.body: Opus made this overnight" and it’s literally just modded GTA with a filter, be fr. 💀 Best I've ever actually one-shotted is a mid Pong clone, and even that needed another prompt just to fix the physics.

comments.author: wirthmore
comments.body:
I have a functional game, on the market with years worth of assets made. 

As an experiment I had Fable 5.2 take in all of those assets and make a simple game in a different genre out of them. (My prompt was more involved than that…) But even with all of the assets readily available, I still had to iterate. Some of the iteration was Claude saying “this should go that way”, me saying ok, then the result was complete trash and the next few iterations were me undoing Claude’s design choices.

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body:
>Just for the sake of experimentation, has anyone here successfully one shotted anything worth playing?

I've been asking this same question to some of the avid vibe-design-and-coding defenders here, who claim AAAs that took years to make could now be made in days/weeks. I still haven't gotten a single example.

For now, we mostly get copies that look and play worse than the game they're trying to copy. And most of the time it's just some random scene you can move around in, which hardly even qualifies as a game.

These tools have amazing potential, but overselling them will just hurt their reputation in front of the world.

comments.author: Advanced_Invite9435
comments.body:
We should start asking each other if our ai game 'passes as a real game'


'Oh yeah your game totally passes, like all the gamer bros are gonna wanna piece of it'

comments.author: Post-reality
comments.body: I am spending tons of $$$ working on my game for 18 hours per day for 45 days already, and it may take 1-3 years for a closed beta. I think most people on here just try to create copycats & reskins of existing games, if not just casual games for mobile games.  Real, high-quality games still take years of development.

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body: It's classic hype train noise, stay focus on your game, build it thoughtfully and make it feels right \_and\_ fun.

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: Yeah, the one shot thing sets totally wrong expectations. every AI game i've seen that's actually fun to play took weeks of iterating and playtesting, the first prompt is like 5% of it
